name: Lesson 5 · Asking: W-questions and yes/no questions

cards.note: W-questions: the question word, then the verb. wer asks about a person. The question word comes first, the verb second.
W-questions: the question word, then the verb. wer: who. Not to be confused with wo, which means where.
W-questions: the question word, then the verb. wer is the subject here, so the verb takes the er form: kommt.
W-questions: the question word, then the verb. was asks about a thing.
W-questions: the question word, then the verb. was first, the verb second, then du: no do-helper.
W-questions: the question word, then the verb. The stem kost- ends in -t, so er takes -et: kostet.
W-questions: the question word, then the verb. The verb comes second, right after the question word.
W-questions: the question word, then the verb. wo asks where something or someone is.
W-questions: the question word, then the verb. wo + ist: where is.
W-questions: the question word, then the verb. wo: the place where something is.

cards.front: I have a question: **where** is the station?
cards.back: Ich habe eine Frage: **Wo** ist der Bahnhof?
cards.note: W-questions: the question word, then the verb. A full question after a colon starts with a capital letter.
W-questions: the question word, then the verb. woher is where from in one word, and it stays together at the front.
W-questions: the question word, then the verb. wohin asks for a direction, where to; wo is only for where something is.
W-questions: the question word, then the verb. gehen asks wohin, not wo: the movement needs the -hin.
W-questions: the question word, then the verb. German asks how you are called: wie, not was.
W-questions: the question word, then the verb. The stem ends in ß, so du adds only -t: du heißt.
W-questions: the question word, then the verb. er heißt: the same form as du, because the stem already ends in ß.
W-questions: the question word, then the verb. Wie heißt…? asks for a name: literally how is she called.

cards.front: How do you **like** the flat? (one friend)
cards.note: W-questions: the question word, then the verb. The stem ends in -d, so du takes -est. Wie findest du…? asks what someone thinks of something.
W-questions: the question word, then the verb. wie before an adjective: how old, how big.
W-questions: the question word, then the verb. wie + adjective, then the verb second.
W-questions: the question word, then the verb. wann asks about time. Not wenn, which is a different word.
W-questions: the question word, then the verb. wann first, the verb second, the subject after it.
W-questions: the question word, then the verb. warum: why. nicht still goes to the end.

cards.front: **Why** are you buying a computer? (one friend)
cards.note: W-questions: the question word, then the verb. warum first, then the verb, then du, then the rest.
Yes/no questions: the verb first. In a yes/no question the verb comes first, before the subject.
Yes/no questions: the verb first. No do-helper: the verb itself opens the question.
Yes/no questions: the verb first. The verb first, then Sie: wohnen Sie.
Yes/no questions: the verb first. ist first, then the subject die Wohnung.
Yes/no questions: the verb first. English needs does; German just moves the verb to the front.
Yes/no questions: the verb first. ihr kommt becomes kommt ihr in the question.
Yes/no questions: the verb first. The du form keeps its -st when it moves to the front.
Yes/no questions: the verb first. The verb first, then Sie.
Yes/no questions: the verb first. The verb first: lernst du.
Yes/no questions: the verb first. ist first; die Lehrerin is the subject.
Yes/no questions: the verb first. To say yes to a negative question, German uses doch; ja would sound like agreeing with the not.

cards.front: Don't you have time? – **Yes**, I do!
cards.back: Hast du keine Zeit? – **Doch**, ich habe Zeit!
cards.note: Yes/no questions: the verb first. doch contradicts the negative: yes, I do have time.

cards.front: Is the cinema expensive? – **No**, it is cheap.
cards.back: Ist das Kino teuer? – **Nein**, es ist billig.
cards.note: Yes/no questions: the verb first. A positive question gets ja or nein; doch is only for negative ones.
